_meta.description: 10 Progressive demo scenarios for the kb-workspace Opal Consultant UI. Each scenario drives a Q1 → Answer → Q2 → Answer flow. The `cmsFields` objects map directly to CMS content type properties defined in /cms/*.tsx.

scenarios.title: Rental Reimbursement
scenarios.q1: John's car is going into the shop for hail repairs — what does his Florida personal auto policy cover for a rental while it's out?

a1.headline: Rental Reimbursement: Active
a1.summary: Platinum tier rental reimbursement is included. Daily limit and max duration apply.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Rental reimbursement coverage pays for a temporary vehicle while your insured car is being repaired due to a covered comprehensive or collision loss.
cmsFields.DeductibleRules: Rental benefit begins the day after the vehicle is dropped off for repairs. The standard deductible on the underlying claim still applies separately.
cmsFields.BenefitDetails:
• Daily limit: $50/day
  • Maximum duration: 30 days
  • Preferred network: Enterprise, Hertz

scenarios.q2: Can we get the rental authorized today before the repair estimate comes in?

a2.headline: Pre-Authorization Available
a2.summary: A 24-hour pre-authorization window is available before the repair estimate is submitted.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Rental pre-authorization can be issued up to 24 hours before the repair facility submits an estimate. The shop must confirm vehicle drop-off before the rental clock starts.
cmsFields.Steps:
1. Confirm vehicle drop-off date with repair facility
  2. Request pre-authorization code from claims representative
  3. Customer books rental at preferred network location

scenarios.title: Storm / Tree Damage
scenarios.q1: A neighbor's tree fell on John's fence during last night's hail storm in Orlando — does his Florida homeowners policy cover the fence damage and debris removal?

a1.headline: Coverage Found: Other Structures
a1.summary: Fence damage from storm falls under Other Structures coverage. Debris removal has a separate sub-limit.

cmsFields.SourceLabel: Homeowners Policy — Other Structures + FL Storm Endorsement
cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Damage to fences, detached garages, and other structures caused by a windstorm or hail event is covered under the Other Structures portion of the homeowners policy at 10% of the dwelling coverage limit.
cmsFields.DeductibleRules: The standard homeowners deductible applies. Florida policies with a separate wind/hail deductible will apply that amount instead of the all-peril deductible.
cmsFields.Exceptions: Debris Removal: Reasonable costs to remove the fallen tree are covered up to $500 per occurrence (or 5% of the dwelling limit, whichever is less), separate from the structural repair limit.
cmsFields.StateDisclosure: FL: Hurricane deductible does not apply to this claim unless the storm was officially designated a named hurricane at time of loss.

scenarios.q2: The tree also landed on his car in the driveway — is that the same claim or a separate one?

a2.headline: Separate Claim Required: Auto Comprehensive
a2.summary: Vehicle damage is NOT covered under Homeowners. Auto Comprehensive covers it — a separate claim and deductible apply.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Homeowners policies exclude coverage for damage to motor vehicles, even when parked on the insured premises and damaged by a covered peril.
cmsFields.Exceptions: Vehicle damage from the same storm event must be filed as a separate comprehensive claim under the auto policy. A separate auto deductible applies.

scenarios.title: Personal Property Theft from Vehicle
scenarios.q1: John's laptop and camera gear were stolen from his car in a parking garage — does his personal auto or homeowners policy cover the stolen items?

a1.headline: Auto: Not Covered — Home: Covered
a1.summary: Personal property stolen from a vehicle is excluded under auto. Homeowners off-premises personal property rider applies.

cmsFields.SourceLabel: Auto Policy — Personal Property Exclusion Clause
cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Personal auto policies do not cover personal belongings stolen from an insured vehicle. Items such as laptops, cameras, and clothing are excluded from auto comprehensive coverage.
cmsFields.Exceptions: Coverage for stolen personal property from a vehicle falls under the Homeowners off-premises personal property coverage, typically at 10% of the personal property limit. Depreciation may apply.

scenarios.q2: His camera kit is worth about $4,000 — is that within the standard off-premises limit or does he need a scheduled endorsement?

a2.headline: Scheduled Endorsement Recommended
a2.summary: The standard off-premises cap may be insufficient. A Scheduled Personal Articles endorsement offers agreed-value coverage with no depreciation.

cmsFields.SourceLabel: Homeowners Policy — Personal Property Coverage + SPA Endorsement
cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Standard off-premises personal property coverage is 10% of the total personal property limit. For a $200,000 personal property coverage, this cap is $20,000 — but individual high-value items may have sub-limits (e.g., cameras typically capped at $1,500 per item).
cmsFields.RecommendationRationale: A Scheduled Personal Articles (SPA) endorsement covers items at agreed value with no depreciation and no deductible. Requires a recent appraisal or purchase receipt for items over $2,500.

scenarios.title: Roadside Assistance
scenarios.q1: John's car just broke down on I-4 in Florida — does his personal auto policy include roadside assistance and how does he request a tow?

a1.headline: Roadside Assistance: Active
a1.summary: Platinum tier includes full roadside assistance. Towing, lockout, fuel delivery, and battery jump are covered.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Roadside Assistance is included at no additional cost on Platinum tier policies. Coverage includes: towing (up to $100), lockout service, fuel delivery, battery jump-start, and flat tire change.
cmsFields.DeductibleRules: No deductible applies to Roadside Assistance calls. Each service request is logged; more than 3 calls per policy period may result in surcharge review at renewal.

scenarios.q2: The nearest network shop is 22 miles away — what happens if the tow goes over the coverage limit?

a2.headline: Tow Overage: Member Responsibility or Reimbursement
a2.summary: The $100 towing limit covers the first portion. Member pays the overage but can submit for reimbursement within 72 hours.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: The $100 towing benefit applies toward the total tow cost. Any amount above $100 is the member's responsibility at the time of service.
cmsFields.Exceptions: If the member paid the full tow cost out-of-pocket, a reimbursement of up to $100 can be requested within 72 hours by submitting the receipt through the claims portal or calling the claims line.

scenarios.title: Snapshot / Telematics
scenarios.q1: Are there any Progressive telematics tools that could lower John's personal auto premium based on his driving behavior?

a1.headline: Snapshot® Available
a1.summary: Snapshot® usage-based program offers an immediate participation discount plus a behavior-based renewal discount.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Snapshot® is Progressive's usage-based insurance program. A small plug-in device or mobile app tracks driving behaviors over 6 months. Participation earns an immediate discount at enrollment; driving behavior determines the renewal discount (or surcharge).
cmsFields.ProgramDetails:
• Immediate participation discount upon enrollment
  • Renewal discount based on: braking patterns, time of day, mileage
  • Average savings: $146/yr for good drivers

scenarios.q2: He drives mostly on weekends — will that help or hurt his Snapshot score?

a2.headline: Weekend Driving: Favorable Profile
a2.summary: Low mileage and weekend-dominant driving are positive scoring factors. Hard braking and late-night miles are the primary negatives.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Snapshot® scoring rewards low-mileage, daytime driving. Weekend-only drivers typically score well because they avoid high-risk commute windows and accumulate fewer overall miles.
cmsFields.Exceptions: Factors that may hurt the score: hard braking events (most impactful), driving between midnight–4am, and rapid acceleration. A profile with primarily weekend, daytime, low-mileage driving avoids all three primary negatives.

scenarios.title: Missing Discounts
scenarios.q1: What discounts is John currently missing on his Florida home and auto bundle that he'd qualify for today?

a1.headline: 3 Unenrolled Discounts Found
a1.summary: Three discounts are available but not currently applied: Snapshot®, paperless billing, and pay-in-full.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Based on John's current policy profile, three discounts are eligible but not yet applied to his bundle.

DiscountItems.name: Paperless Billing
DiscountItems.requirement: Switch to electronic statements and billing notices

DiscountItems.name: Pay-in-Full
DiscountItems.requirement: Pay full policy term premium at renewal

scenarios.q2: He wants to switch to paperless and pay in full right now — can we apply both on this call?

a2.headline: Both Discounts Applied
a2.summary: Paperless billing and pay-in-full can both be applied immediately and take effect at the next billing cycle.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Both the paperless billing discount and pay-in-full discount can be applied during an active service call. Changes take effect at the next billing cycle or renewal date, whichever is sooner.
cmsFields.Steps:
1. Confirm customer's email address for paperless enrollment
  2. Process pay-in-full payment for remaining balance
  3. Discounts will appear on the next policy document
  4. Confirm updated projected premium with customer

scenarios.title: Liability After Accident
scenarios.q1: John was in a fender bender yesterday and the other driver is now claiming a back injury — what are his personal auto liability limits and what should we advise him?

a1.headline: Liability Coverage: Active
a1.summary: Bodily Injury and Property Damage limits confirmed. Consultant guidance issued for injury claim scenario.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: John's Platinum auto policy includes the following liability limits: Bodily Injury $100,000 per person / $300,000 per occurrence; Property Damage $100,000 per occurrence; Medical Payments $5,000 per person.
cmsFields.DeductibleRules: No deductible applies to liability claims paid to third parties. The liability coverage protects John against damages he is legally obligated to pay.
cmsFields.Exceptions: Consultant guidance: Advise John not to admit fault or discuss the incident with the other party directly. Document all available evidence. A claims representative will be assigned within 24 hours of opening the claim.

scenarios.q2: He hasn't filed a claim yet — how do we open one and what information does he need to have ready?

a2.headline: Claim Intake: Liability
a2.summary: Walk the consultant through the required information checklist and open the liability claim.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: To open a liability claim (FNOL), the following information must be collected before the claim can be routed to a claims representative.
cmsFields.Steps:
1. Date, time, and location of the incident
  2. Other driver's name, contact, and insurance information
  3. Police report number (if applicable)
  4. Photos of vehicle damage and scene
  5. Names and contact info of any witnesses
cmsFields.Exceptions: If a bodily injury is being claimed, the file is automatically escalated to the Injury Claims team. Timeline: initial contact from claims representative within 24 hours.

scenarios.title: Burst Pipe / Water Damage
scenarios.q1: A pipe burst in John's Florida home and flooded the finished basement — does his homeowners policy cover the water damage to the structure and his furniture?

a1.headline: Covered: Sudden Water Damage / Excluded: Flood
a1.summary: Sudden and accidental water damage from a burst pipe is covered. Flood damage from external water is excluded and requires separate NFIP coverage.

cmsFields.SourceLabel: Homeowners Policy — Water Damage Coverage + FL Endorsement
cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Sudden and accidental discharge of water from a burst pipe is covered under the dwelling and personal property portions of the homeowners policy. Damage to both the structure (finished basement walls, flooring) and furniture is eligible.
cmsFields.DeductibleRules: The standard homeowners deductible applies. Florida policies may carry a separate wind/water endorsement — confirm which deductible applies based on the loss cause.
cmsFields.Exceptions: Flood Exclusion: Damage caused by surface water, storm surge, or water that enters from outside the structure is excluded. A separate National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) policy or private flood policy is required for flood coverage.
cmsFields.StateDisclosure: FL: Sinkhole activity is a separate disclosure. If the burst pipe was caused by or associated with ground movement, a sinkhole inspection may be required before the claim is processed.

scenarios.q2: He wants to know if he should also look at a separate flood policy given he's in Central Florida.

a2.headline: Flood Coverage Advisory: Central Florida
a2.summary: NFIP and private flood options are available. His zip code's FEMA flood zone determines risk level and pricing.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: Central Florida (Orlando metro) includes a mix of FEMA flood zones ranging from low-risk (Zone X) to moderate-risk (Zone AE). Even Zone X properties can experience flooding from heavy rain events — NFIP data shows 25% of flood claims come from low-to-moderate risk areas.
cmsFields.RecommendationRationale: Options available: NFIP (government-backed, up to $250,000 dwelling / $100,000 contents, typically 30-day waiting period); Private flood (higher limits, faster binding, broader coverage). Recommend confirming the property's FEMA flood zone before quoting.

scenarios.title: Umbrella Upsell
scenarios.q1: John has a Platinum home and auto bundle — does he have enough liability coverage or is he a good candidate for umbrella insurance?

a1.headline: Umbrella Coverage Recommended
a1.summary: Current liability limits may fall short of estimated asset exposure. A $1M umbrella policy fills the gap at low monthly cost.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: John's current liability exposure: auto BI at $100K/$300K and homeowners liability at $300K. A serious auto accident with injuries or a premises liability suit could exceed these limits, leaving personal assets at risk.
cmsFields.RecommendationRationale: A $1,000,000 personal umbrella policy provides excess liability above auto and home limits, plus coverage for personal injury (libel, slander), and worldwide incidents. Estimated cost: $15–$25/month for most profiles. Requires underlying auto and home to meet minimum liability thresholds (already met at Platinum).

scenarios.q2: What does umbrella actually cover that his home and auto policies don't already handle?

a2.headline: Umbrella Gap Explained
a2.summary: Umbrella extends liability beyond existing policy limits and covers scenarios that home and auto exclude outright.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition:
What umbrella adds beyond auto and home:

  • Excess liability — activates when auto or home liability limits are exhausted
  • Personal injury — libel, slander, wrongful eviction (excluded by home/auto)
  • Worldwide coverage — incidents outside the US not covered by domestic auto/home
  • Rental property liability — if John ever rents out property
cmsFields.Exceptions: Umbrella does NOT cover: business activities, intentional acts, or vehicle damage (those stay with the underlying policies).

scenarios.title: College Student Transition
scenarios.q1: John's daughter is moving to Ohio for college and taking the second car — what changes need to be made to his Florida auto and homeowners policies?

a1.headline: Life Event: Dependent Going to College
a1.summary: Auto garaging address must update to Ohio. Homeowners off-premises covers dorm contents up to the policy cap.

cmsFields.SourceLabel: Life Events Guide — Dependent College Enrollment
cmsFields.CoreDefinition: When a dependent moves to another state for college with an insured vehicle, two policy changes are typically required: (1) the vehicle's garaging address must update to the college state, and (2) premium and coverage terms may shift based on the new rating territory.
cmsFields.DeductibleRules: Ohio rates may differ from Florida rates. The garaging update triggers a mid-term premium adjustment. No deductible change required unless the customer elects to update coverage.
cmsFields.Exceptions:
Homeowners: The daughter's belongings in the dorm are covered under the off-premises personal property provision (typically 10% of personal property limit). Electronics may have a sub-limit — confirm if a SPA endorsement is needed for high-value items.

Vehicle registration: Ohio requires vehicles principally garaged in-state to be registered in Ohio within 30 days.

scenarios.q2: She's a full-time student — does that qualify her for any discount back on John's policy?

a2.headline: Good Student Discount: Eligible
a2.summary: Full-time student with qualifying GPA is eligible for the Good Student Discount, applying at next renewal.

cmsFields.CoreDefinition: The Good Student Discount applies to drivers aged 16–25 who are enrolled full-time and maintain a GPA of 3.0 or higher (or equivalent class rank).
cmsFields.Exceptions: Discount applies at the next renewal after eligibility documentation is submitted. Required documents: current official transcript or honor roll letter (must show GPA ≥ 3.0 or rank in top 20% of class). Discount typically ranges from 5–25% of the rated driver's portion of the premium.
